The filters can be applied to other views if the same fields are involved (or even if they are not... we should be able to just apply random filters if we want )
They should probably update immediately.  If we allow old and new, it will be a mess to determine how to change each on its own (or how to udpate the snapshot)
Reuse or keep open.  either is fine.  Probably make it easy for the user to "duplciate" a view. Comparison is harder isnce it probalbe requires side by side.  don't worry about that for now,

claims.statement: People can create and revise analysis through runtime configuration
A project holds shared definitions and several views for specific analysis tasks
A sales overview opens a store detail view with an active store parameter
A server can collect changes and persist them to disk or a database
The package accepts one row array and one saved settings object per mounted workspace
Switching analyses and overview-to-detail navigation take priority over comparison.
The representative project contains products, orders, and customers as separate sources with different row counts.
Automatic save, explicit Save, and persistence of temporary selections remain undecided.
Reusable filters store fields, thresholds, and selected values and can apply beyond visible chart fields.
Shared field definitions and color scales should update dependent views immediately without snapshots.
Users can duplicate saved tabs; local chart and filter edits stay independent. Comparison is deferred.
Users and developers can create parameterized views and connections.
Views combine source tables through lookups.
A dedicated Filters section shows conditions without requiring their fields on visible charts.
claims.resolution: Initial saved tabs reuse existing chart and Rows filter controls. Dedicated filter collection remains later work.

claims.statement: Current project and task views use one source. Multi-source lookups move to their own initiative.
History checkpoints distinguish project shared definitions from view-local settings.
Initial scope is multiple saved views on tabs over one source; a view contains chart definitions and filters.
Save edits automatically to local storage; ideally retain all client state including the source and session.
Reliable Undo and a time travel slider recover previous state and distinguish view changes from filter changes.
Parameterized overview-to-detail navigation moves to a separate follow-up; filter inheritance remains unresolved.
Execution uses project settings checkpoints, read-only preview, and explicit restore as a reversible default.

human_questions.resolution: Project settings timeline is the execution default; retain 50 checkpoints. Larger imports need further measurement.

shape.appetite: One source, saved tabs, automatic local persistence, Undo and categorized time travel.
shape.problem: One saved analysis cannot retain several independent chart-and-filter investigations.
shape.recommended_shape: Named tabs own charts, layout, and filters. One project owns source and shared definitions. Autosave meaningful client state locally; preview and restore categorized historical settings. Split parameterized navigation into a follow-up.
success_moves: Prove two independent tabs before connection authoring.
Reuse saved settings and explicit restore; keep callbacks out of continuous restore loops.
Store source rows once; keep history as settings checkpoints.
Categorize chart/filter/shared changes while restoring consistent snapshots.
Measure storage size and inject save/restore failures before promising full local retention.
Keep preview read-only and retain displaced present when restoring history.

first_proof.question: Can two chart-and-filter views survive switching and reload, then recover earlier edits?
first_proof.artifact: Fixed order fixture with Sales and Returns tabs, distinct filters, and labeled chart/filter history entries.
first_proof.observation: Independent charts, counts, layouts, active tab and retained history restore; preview does not overwrite saved present.
first_proof.decision_rule: Continue only if tab retention and history recovery work without navigation; resolve storage limits before larger data.

uncertainties: Local storage capacity for larger imports
shape.smaller_counterproposal: Tabs and autosave alone are the first visible slice, but do not satisfy the required Undo and slider outcome.
shape.source_of_truth: One project source and shared current definitions; each tab owns local charts/layout/filters. Checkpoints store consistent project settings.

superseded_shape.appetite: Products, orders, and customers project with lookup-driven overview/detail, duplication, and a Filters section.
superseded_shape.recommended_shape: Use a products, orders, and customers project as the representative workflow. Support named task views, overview-to-detail connections, and easy view duplication. Put genuinely shared field definitions and color scales at project scope so changes reach dependent views immediately.

uncertainties: Filter field absent from all sources: expose applicability; exact handling pending

review.remaining_weaknesses: Lookup behavior must make missing and repeated matches understandable. The Filters section resolves visibility, but hidden chart fields still differ from fields unavailable from all sources. Applicability must remain clear so the interface does not misrepresent a restriction. Save behavior remains explicitly undecided.
review.most_likely_bad_outcome: Views become isolated dashboards over separate tables, and supposedly reusable filters silently stop working when the data changes.
